name: Wisconsin
summary: Statutes, constitution, session laws, Administrative Code and Register all sit on docs.legis.wisconsin.gov (Legislative Reference Bureau), and each is constructible from a citation through the /document/... redirector (e.g. /document/statutes/802.06(2)(a)6., /document/administrativecode/DHS%20110.04, /document/wisconsinconstitution/I,9); the statutes are certified under s. 35.18. Civil procedure, evidence and appellate procedure are statutes (chs. 801-847, 901-911, 809); Supreme Court Rules (SCR, incl. ch. 20 professional conduct) are per-chapter PDFs on wicourts.gov. Case law: wicourts.gov serves Supreme Court and Court of Appeals slip opinions (published and unpublished) from 1995 as PDFs, found by plain GET searches that accept a public-domain citation (pdcNo=2024 WI 13), docket number, party name or date range. Petition-for-review dispositions are findable by docket number (scorder.jsp order PDFs and the bimonthly disposition tables); WebFetch is gated on built wicourts URLs, so use fetch_doc.py.

citation_patterns.label: Wisconsin Supreme Court Rules (bare "SCR NN.NN", shared with Nevada)
Wisconsin Court of Appeals public-domain citation

citation_map.notes: Wisconsin style (SCR 80.02, Wis. Stat. § 809.19) cites cases in public-domain form first: '2024 WI 13, ¶ 22, 4xx Wis. 2d ___, ___ N.W.3d ___'; public-domain citations exist for decisions from 1994/1995 onward (wicourts listings start 1995). Court of Appeals opinions are 'WI App'. The bimonthly Supreme Court disposition tables are themselves assigned a 'YYYY WI N' number (e.g. 2026 WI 33), so a 'review denied, YYYY WI N' cite resolves to a table, not an opinion. Statute sections are always CHAPTER.SECTION (no hyphens); 'Wis. Stat. §§ 893.52-893.55' is a range — the regex takes the first section. Wisconsin writes subunits with spaces ('802.06 (2) (a) 6.'); strip spaces for the URL. Appellate procedure (ch. 809) is cited as 'Wis. Stat. § (Rule) 809.62' or 'Wis. Stat. Rule 809.62'; civil procedure (chs. 801-847) and evidence (chs. 901-911) are ordinary statutes. Bare 'Rule 809.xx' and bare 'review denied' are context_required. SCR ch. 20 (professional conduct) uses a colon ('SCR 20:1.7'), which is distinctive; other SCR chapters use a dot ('SCR 22.03(2)') and route here bare only with a subunit parenthetical and a known Wisconsin SCR chapter number (Nevada also has 'SCR' rules). 'Register, Month YYYY, No. NNN' history notes cite the Administrative Register. Unpublished Court of Appeals opinions authored after July 1, 2009 may be cited for persuasive value with the form 'No. 2025AP1919, unpublished slip op. ¶ 12 (WI App Oct. 15, 2026)' (Wis. Stat. § 809.23(3)). CourtListener ids 'wis' and 'wisctapp' are from memory, unverified. Cross-routing caution: Nevada's record has a bare 'SCR \d+' pattern that also matches Wisconsin's practitioner form 'SCR 20:1.7' / 'SCR 22.03'; the colon form ('20:1.7') is uniquely Wisconsin, so route 'SCR NN:N.N' here. The colon form 'SCR 20:1.7' identifies Wisconsin; bare 'SCR NN.NN' is shared with Nevada's Supreme Court Rules and routes here only once Wisconsin is established. 'Wis. Stat. ch. 893' (chapter cite) is captured by the statutes pattern's chapter group and routes to the chapter PDF/page. The prose form 'section 893.54 of the statutes' (Wisconsin acts' drafting style) has no state marker and is context_required.

sources.title: Wisconsin Statutes & Annotations (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)
sources.official_status_evidence: Every page footer: 'Published and certified under s. 35.18.' Wis. Stat. § 35.18(1)(b) requires the LRB to publish an updated electronic version with a notice that it is certified under sub. (2)(b). Not a UELMA authentication.
sources.coverage: Current 2023-24 Wisconsin Statutes with annotations, updated continuously; prior biennial editions under /statutes/prior/.

access.pattern_rules: section = CHAPTER.SECTION exactly as cited (893.54, 940.01, 180.0302, 802.06). Optional subunits appended with spaces removed, keeping the trailing period on numbered subdivisions: Wis. Stat. § 802.06(2)(a)6. → /document/statutes/802.06(2)(a)6. The /document/ URL 302-redirects to the canonical path /statutes/statutes/{chapter}/{subchapter_roman_lower}/{section_suffix}[/{sub}/...] (893.54 → /statutes/statutes/893/v/54; 940.01 → /940/i/01; 180.0302 → /180/iii/0302; 802.06(2)(a)6. → /802/06/2/a/6). Do NOT build the canonical path yourself: chapters with subchapters need the Roman subchapter segment (/893/54 returns 404). The page is a scrolling window holding the target section plus neighbouring sections (893.54 page holds 893.52-893.55, ~31K chars).
access.navigation: Index lists every chapter with title (no section ranges, but section numbers encode the chapter, so no hop is needed).

automation.robots_txt: User-agent * Disallow: /frame, /frame/, /scroll/, /feed/, /doc/feed/, /breadcrumbs/, /preferences, /search, one LRB PDF. /document/, /statutes/, /code/, /constitution/ allowed.
automation.notes: WebFetch on a built /document/ URL was gated once (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED) and worked in the independent check, returning the section text but not the currency footer; the search-surfaced canonical URL /statutes/statutes/893/V/54 was cut mid-893.55 ('Loading...') and showed an older snapshot (Act 170, May 22, 2026) than the live page read by the script (Act 247, Oct. 1, 2026). Take the currency footer from fetch_doc.py only. /search is robots-disallowed: never use the site search.

automation.notes: fetch_doc.py: root returns HTML with 0 extractable chars (JS shell); guessed /caseDetails.do?caseNo= and /appealHistory.xsl paths 404. Not tried further.

hazards: JavaScript-only

absent.evidence: wicourts listing: final version appears in the bound official reports; PDFs carry slip pagination and ¶ numbers only (2024 WI 13 PDF).
scopin.jsp and caopin.jsp with begin_date 01/01/1994-12/31/1994: 'Sorry, no records found'; 1995 returns rows.

script_candidates.why: Plain GET search scopin.jsp / caopin.jsp by public-domain cite (pdcNo), docket, party or date, returning rows with seqNo PDF links: a script can resolve '2024 WI 13' or '2020 WI App 34' to the PDF deterministically.
scorder.jsp?docket_number= returns review orders for the decision below by docket; disposition-table PDFs are greppable by docket.
/document/{collection}/{cite} redirector resolves statutes, admin code, constitution and acts from the citation.

corpus_candidates.why: SCR ch. 20 Preamble-20:1.18: 107 pages, 298,902 chars; beyond the fetch tool's window.
Chapter PDFs of the certified statutes run to 448K chars (ch. 893); HTML per-section route already works, so ingest only chapters heavily used (801-847, 809, 901-911).

open_questions: Bulk statute/admin-code download (XML/zip) from the LRB not found; not searched exhaustively.
WebFetch is gated on built docs.legis and wicourts URLs; the docs.legis HTML route was confirmed only through a search-surfaced URL, and it served an older snapshot than the live page.
Official status of the online Administrative Code (s. 35.93) and Constitution not confirmed; Wisconsin UELMA status not checked.
Opinion search by reporter cite (cite_type='Wis. 2d' / 'N.W.2d' with cite_volume/cite_page) not confirmed working.
Start year of scorder.jsp order coverage and of the online disposition-table archive not determined.
Justia statute and case URL patterns each proven on one citation only.
Circuit court local rules location not researched.
Bare 'EmRNNNN' cites have no deterministic issue lookup in the Administrative Register; the only route is scanning that year's issues.
